items.question: How can one attain liberation while experiencing enjoyment?
premises: Liberation is obtained through enjoyment
This occurs after hearing from the guru's mouth
The teaching received is supreme
items.inference: Hearing the supreme teaching from the guru allows one to attain liberation even through enjoyment.
uncertainties: The exact referent of parām is contextually implied as the supreme teaching or knowledge.
items.plain_english: Having heard the supreme teaching from the guru's mouth, one attains liberation through enjoyment.

items.question: What form of Krodhīśa is to be visualized in this context?
premises: Krodhīśa is the object of visualization
He is mounted on blood
He is marked by Dhūmra-Bhairavī
items.inference: The visualization depicts Krodhīśa mounted on blood and associated with Dhūmra-Bhairavī.
uncertainties: The precise symbolic meaning of kṣataja in this context is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: Visualize Krodhīśa mounted on blood and marked by Dhūmra-Bhairavī.

items.question: Does any knowledge in the three worlds equal the one-syllable knowledge?
premises: The comparison concerns knowledge equal to one syllable
The scope is the three worlds
No such equal knowledge exists
items.inference: There is no knowledge in the three worlds equal to the one-syllable knowledge.
items.plain_english: O beloved, there is no knowledge in the three worlds equal to the one-syllable knowledge.

items.question: What other supreme teaching is the speaker about to declare?
premises: The speaker introduces another topic
The speaker will declare it
The topic is the supreme southern Kālikā
items.inference: The speaker will now declare the teaching of the supreme southern Kālikā.
items.plain_english: Now I shall declare another teaching: the supreme southern Kālikā.

items.question: What three-syllable mantra is declared beginning with the māyā-seed?
premises: The māyā-seed comes first
A three-syllable mantra follows
This mantra is declared
items.inference: A three-syllable mantra beginning with the māyā-seed is declared.
uncertainties: The remaining syllables of the three-syllable mantra are not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: O fair one, then the three-syllable mantra beginning with the māyā-seed is declared.

items.question: What additional fruit-giving three-syllable mantra is declared here?
premises: Another three-syllable mantra is declared
It is as previously stated
It gives fruit
items.inference: Another previously stated three-syllable mantra is declared as fruit-giving.
uncertainties: The exact form of this mantra is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: O beloved, another three-syllable mantra, as previously stated, is declared to be fruit-giving.

items.question: What specific benefit does this three-syllable mantra grant?
premises: This mantra is three-syllable
It is addressed to the goddess
It grants the fruits of all desires
items.inference: This three-syllable mantra grants the fulfillment of all desires.
items.plain_english: O goddess, this three-syllable mantra indeed grants the fruits of all desires.

items.question: What restrictions or faults do not apply to this mantra practice?
premises: There is no time restriction here
There is no fault related to enemy or friend and so on
Both absences apply to this practice
items.inference: This mantra practice is free from time restrictions and faults concerning enemies, friends, and others.
items.plain_english: Here there is no restriction of time, nor any fault concerning enemy, friend, and so forth.

items.question: When and where is recitation of this mantra considered auspicious?
premises: Recitation may be done by day or by night
Recitation is auspicious everywhere
No temporal or spatial limitation is imposed
items.inference: Recitation of this mantra is auspicious at any time and in any place.
items.plain_english: Whether by day or by night, recitation is auspicious everywhere.

items.question: What result does a person obtain through this knowledge even with enjoyment?
premises: A person uses this knowledge
Enjoyment is present
Liberation is obtained
items.inference: By this knowledge, a person obtains liberation even while experiencing enjoyment.
items.plain_english: Even through enjoyment, a person obtains liberation by this knowledge.

items.question: How does this knowledge and its recitation compare to all others?
premises: No knowledge is similar to this knowledge
No recitation is similar to this recitation
Both comparisons assert uniqueness
items.inference: This knowledge and its recitation are without equal.
items.plain_english: There is no knowledge similar to this, and no recitation similar to this.

items.question: How emphatically does the speaker affirm the truth of this declaration?
premises: The word truth is repeated three times
The speaker states it with truth foremost
The speaker personally affirms it
items.inference: The speaker emphatically and personally affirms the declaration as true.
items.plain_english: Truth, truth, and again truth—I say this with truth foremost.

items.question: What topic will the speaker now explain in brief form?
premises: The speaker introduces a new topic
The explanation will be brief
The topic is the supreme method of worship
items.inference: The speaker will now briefly explain the supreme method of worship.
items.plain_english: Now I shall briefly tell the supreme method of worship.

items.question: Into what three categories is worship classified in this teaching?
premises: Worship is declared to be threefold
The categories are daily, occasional, and optional
This classification defines types of worship
items.inference: Worship is classified into daily, occasional, and optional types.
items.plain_english: And worship is declared to be threefold: daily, occasional, and optional.

items.question: What seer and meter are assigned to this knowledge?
premises: Bhairava is declared the seer of this knowledge
The meter is stated as uṣṇik
These are ritual assignments
items.inference: The seer of this knowledge is Bhairava and its meter is uṣṇik.
items.plain_english: Bhairava is declared the seer of this, and uṣṇik is stated as the meter.

items.question: For what purposes is the application of this knowledge prescribed?
premises: The application of the knowledge is specified
It applies to the four aims of human life
This defines its ritual scope
items.inference: The application of this knowledge is for the four aims of human life.
items.plain_english: The application of this knowledge is indeed for the four aims of human life.

items.question: Under what condition is worship considered suitable for a malevolent rite?
premises: Worship is performed without the five purifications
Such worship is considered for abhicāra
The absence of purifications changes its purpose
items.inference: Worship without the five purifications is considered suitable for a malevolent rite.
items.plain_english: Worship without the five purifications is considered for a malevolent rite.

items.question: What purifications are included in the declared five purifications?
premises: Mantra purification is named
Deity purification is named
These are declared as part of the five purifications
items.inference: Mantra purification and deity purification are included among the five purifications.
uncertainties: Only two of the five purifications are explicitly named in this verse.
items.plain_english: Mantra purification and deity purification are thus declared as part of the five purifications.

items.question: What kind of seat should be prepared at the beginning of worship?
premises: A seat should be prepared first
It may be soft
It may be a blanket
items.inference: At the beginning, one should prepare a soft seat or a blanket.
items.plain_english: First one should prepare a seat, either soft or a blanket.

items.question: Why should element purification be performed before worship?
premises: Element purification should be performed
It is done so that one becomes fit for worship
Fitness for worship is the intended result
items.inference: Element purification is performed to make one fit for worship.
items.plain_english: Then one should perform element purification so that one may become fit for worship.

items.question: To whom is the initial obeisance directed in this worship sequence?
premises: The obeisance is made first
It is directed to Śuddhi-Bhairava
Śuddhi-Bhairava is addressed as the seer
items.inference: The initial obeisance is directed to Śuddhi-Bhairava as the seer.
items.plain_english: First, obeisance to Śuddhi-Bhairava, the seer, thus; then proceed.

items.question: Where and to which deity is obeisance assigned in this step?
premises: Obeisance is directed to Mahākālī
Mahākālī is identified as the deity
The assignment is made in the heart
items.inference: Obeisance to Mahākālī, the deity, is assigned in the heart.
items.plain_english: O my beloved, obeisance to Mahākālī, the deity, in the heart.

items.question: For what specific purpose is the application assigned with desire?
premises: The application is stated for poetic skill
It is assigned ritually
It is done with desire
items.inference: The application is assigned with desire for the attainment of poetic skill.
items.plain_english: Having assigned the application for poetic skill, thus, with desire.

items.question: Which bīja syllables are placed on the thumbs and index fingers in this nyāsa?
premises: The syllables oṃ krā are placed on the thumbs
The syllables oṃ krī are associated with the index fingers
This forms part of the ritual placement
items.inference: The nyāsa places oṃ krā on the thumbs and oṃ krī with obeisance on the index fingers.
items.plain_english: Placing oṃ krā on the thumbs, and oṃ krī with obeisance on the index fingers.
